words.story: Chhath is a festival where people thank the Sun god for life and energy. It is biggest in Nepal's Terai region.
customs: 🌅 Stand in rivers at sunset, then again at sunrise
🙏 Offer fruits and sweets to the sun
words.fun_fact: People fast without even drinking water during Chhath!

words.story: Sakela is the main festival of the Rai people, one of Nepal's indigenous groups. It is a dance festival that thanks nature.
words.when: Twice a year — Ubhauli in May (planting season) and Udhauli in December (harvest)
customs: 💃 Dance in a big circle holding hands
words.fun_fact: The dance moves imitate farming — planting and harvesting!

words.story: Losar is the Tibetan New Year, celebrated by Sherpa, Tamang, and Gurung communities in Nepal.
words.fun_fact: There are actually three different Losars — Tamu, Sonam, and Gyalpo!

words.story: Christmas celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ. Christians in Nepal celebrate it, and many others join the fun!
words.fun_fact: Christmas is a public holiday in Nepal!

words.story: Maghi is the Tharu people's New Year festival. The Tharu are one of Nepal's largest indigenous groups.
words.fun_fact: Tharu families pick their community leaders during Maghi!

words.story: Buddha Jayanti celebrates the birth of Gautam Buddha — who was born in Lumbini, Nepal! It also marks his enlightenment.
words.fun_fact: Lumbini, Buddha's birthplace, is a UNESCO World Heritage site!

words.story: Ramadan is the holy month for Muslims, when they fast from sunrise to sunset. It ends with the Eid celebration.
words.fun_fact: The entire month of fasting concludes when the new crescent moon is sighted, marking Eid al-Fitr.
Holi celebrates good beating evil — the colors come from the story of Prahlad and Holika!
words.story: Holi is the festival of colors! Everyone throws bright colored powder and water at each other — friends, family, even strangers. By the end, nobody has clean clothes!

customs: 🐍 Put naga pictures on the door
words.fun_fact: Farmers love snakes — they eat the rats that would destroy the crops!
words.story: Nag Panchami is the day we honor snakes! People stick snake pictures above their doors for protection and offer milk at snake shrines.

words.fun_fact: A king started Gai Jatra to make his sad queen laugh again!
words.story: Gai Jatra is the cow festival! Families who lost someone that year walk a cow through town — or dress up as one. It is a happy day that turns tears into laughter.

words.fun_fact: Legend says the thundering hooves keep a demon trapped underground!
words.story: Ghode Jatra is the horse festival! The Nepal Army puts on amazing horse races and trick riding at Tundikhel in Kathmandu.

customs: 🎋 Help raise the tall ceremonial pole
words.fun_fact: The Kumari is a real young girl who is worshipped as a living goddess!
words.story: Indra Jatra honors Indra, the king of heaven and god of rain. It is Kathmandu's biggest street party — the living goddess Kumari rides through town in her chariot!

customs: 🌙 Stay up all night in prayer
words.fun_fact: More than a million people visit Pashupatinath on this single night!
words.story: Maha Shivaratri is the great night of Lord Shiva! People stay awake all night praying, and huge crowds gather at Pashupatinath temple.

words.fun_fact: 'Sonam' means good merit — the year begins by doing good deeds!
words.story: Sonam Losar is the Tamang people's new year! Families clean the house, wear new clothes, and celebrate with dancing, music, and feasting.

words.fun_fact: Every Tamu Losar year is named after an animal — just like the Chinese zodiac!
words.story: Tamu Losar is the Gurung people's new year! Gurung families gather for traditional dances, drum music, and delicious community feasts.

decks.title: Lyric Breakdowns
decks.theme: What your favorite songs actually mean

words.english: Traditional folk song every Nepali kid grows up hearing. 'Resham' means silk, 'firiri' is the fluttering motion — like silk dancing in the wind. Playful, upbeat, about beauty and joy. Composed by Buddhi Pariyar, collected from Pokhara villages. First recorded at Radio Nepal in 1969, sung by Sunder Shrestha and Dwarika Lal Joshi.

Swoopna Suman × Samir Shrestha (2023). 'However you are.' Key line — 'Je chhau jaso chhau timi, tehi nai ho malai chahine' — 'no matter who you are, you're the one I need.' About loving someone exactly as they are.
Jhapalish (2025, hip-hop). 'May my ex die' — playful, not serious. 'Maros' is slang for 'die,' used jokingly. A diss track for when you're over someone.

Prem Dhoj Pradhan (classic, music by Natikaji). 'The wind blew at Deurali' — Deurali is a mountain pass where travelers rest. Nostalgic, about wind carrying memories through the hills. Makes Nepalis abroad homesick.
Sajjan Raj Vaidya. 'Cheap heart' — 'sasto' means cheap, 'mutu' means heart. About feeling like your love wasn't valued. Sad but beautiful.

Rajan Raj Shiwakoti & Melina Rai (2017, from Dui Rupaiyan). 243M views — the most-watched Nepali video ever. 'Kutu ma kutu' is the sound of chewing something hard; 'supari dana' is areca nut. Offering supari is how you invite someone to a function in Nepali culture — they chew it to accept. Pure celebration.
SD Yogi & Shanti Shree Pariyar (2024, from Khusma). 193M views — fastest Nepali song to 100M. Rukum is a district in western Nepal, Maikot is a village there. A folk-pop love letter to the region.
